## Summary

Rhythm's scheduler is agent-execution state owned by the local desktop API, but the Rhythm MCP server registers `rhythm_create_scheduled_task`, `rhythm_list_scheduled_tasks`, `rhythm_cancel_scheduled_task`, and `rhythm_trigger_now` with `RHYTHM_API_URL` (production) instead of `RHYTHM_AGENT_URL` (normally `http://localhost:4001`).

This makes MCP tooling observe and mutate a different `agent_scheduled_tasks` dataset than the Flutter scheduler UI and the working local `AgentRunner`.

Live investigation on 2026-07-27 found:

- Local API: 30 rows, 17 enabled.
- Production API: 26 rows, 15 enabled.
- Zero shared schedule IDs.
- The local Memory Consolidation row succeeded while the production row with the same name repeatedly failed.

Both surfaces expose `/agent-schedules`; the defect is base-URL routing, not the REST route or table name.

## Likely files

- `apps/mcp_server/src/index.ts`
- `apps/mcp_server/src/tools/agentSchedule.test.ts`
- `apps/mcp_server/src/__tests__/mcp_capabilities_and_tool_registration.test.ts`
- `apps/api_server/src/__tests__/live_e2e_inert_regressions.test.ts` or a new env-gated live MCP scheduler test

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four scheduler MCP tools are registered with `RHYTHM_AGENT_URL`.
- [ ] Scheduler MCP routing is explicitly documented as local agent-execution state, matching memory, sessions, profiles, delegation, approvals, and org-optimizer tools.
- [ ] A falsification test supplies different production and local URLs and proves every scheduler tool calls only the local URL.
- [ ] A live env-gated behavioral test creates a schedule through the MCP surface and observes the same row through local `GET /agent-schedules`.
- [ ] Triggering through MCP updates the local row and never a production row.

## Required validation

- MCP server typecheck/build.
- Focused scheduler MCP tests.
- Env-gated live behavioral test against the isolated dev sandbox described in `AGENTS.md`.
- GitNexus impact analysis before editing and `detect_changes()` before commit.

## Safety / out of scope

- Do not delete, disable, or migrate production scheduler rows in this issue.
- Do not change production-backed task, rhythm, PCO, Gmail, or calendar tool routing.
- Do not expose API tokens in test output.

## Dependencies

None. This should land before production scheduler cleanup so agents stop mutating the wrong store.
title: Route scheduler MCP tools to the local agent server

## Why this is open again

`docs/ai/decisions/2026-07-30-gallery-source-of-truth-is-the-local-mac.md` decided
the local Mac owns the gallery and rejected cloud-hosting artifacts. That decision
predates mobile being a first-class client, and two things have changed since:

1. **Mobile is now a real client**, not a hypothetical one.
2. **The chat now generates media.** With native GPT image generation (#1094),
   a single run produces ~12 PNGs at 0.8–2 MB each, and the video work produces
   ~21 MB MP4s. These are created continuously, not curated by hand.

That old decision's own consequence #3 named the unbuilt piece exactly: *"the
non-trivial part: artifact bytes. Local file paths are not reachable from a
phone."* This issue is that piece, with the store choice reopened.

## The actual constraint

Generated artifacts currently land in `~/.local/share/opencode/tool-output/`
(images, via `image-generation.ts`) and `~/Downloads` + `$TMPDIR` (video). All
are Mac-local paths, unreachable from a phone, and the images are swept after 7
days.

## Options

**A. Paired-gateway streaming — Mac stays authoritative.** Mobile fetches bytes
through the 4002 gateway.
- *For:* no duplication, no upload cost, artifacts stay where produced, existing
  Device-credential + project-scope security model applies directly.
- *Against:* requires the Mac awake and reachable. A user reviewing a poster on
  their phone at church, Mac asleep at the office, sees nothing. For a
  first-class mobile client that is a poor default.

**B. Cloud-hosted on the Synology — both clients read one place.**
- *For:* always available; simple URL space; straightforward mobile download;
  cacheable via Cloudflare.
- *Against:* upload cost per artifact, unbounded storage growth, second copy to
  keep consistent.
- **Important:** put the **bytes on the filesystem or object storage** (a
  Synology share, or MinIO for S3 semantics) and only **metadata in Postgres**.
  Storing 21 MB videos as Postgres BLOBs bloats the DB, inflates every backup,
  and makes range requests painful. Postgres row: id, project, session, mime,
  size, checksum, created_at, storage_key.

**C. Hybrid (recommended).** Local Mac remains where artifacts are produced;
Synology becomes the durable, always-available copy.
- Upload generated media to Synology object storage automatically, with a size
  policy (images always; large video uploaded but previewed via a generated
  thumbnail/poster frame, full file downloaded on demand).
- Mobile reads the cloud copy by default; the paired gateway stays as a
  fast/fresh path when the Mac is reachable.
- Metadata rows in Postgres; bytes addressed by checksum so re-generating the
  same image does not duplicate storage.

Recommendation is C, because it gives mobile an always-available read path
without making the Mac's filesystem the thing a phone depends on — while keeping
the DB free of binaries.

## Things that must be decided, not assumed

- **Retention.** This is the part that bites later. ~12 images + a video per
  creative run grows without bound. Needs a TTL, a per-project quota, or
  explicit pinning. The local dir already self-sweeps at 7 days; the cloud copy
  needs its own answer.
- **Range requests** on the serving route, or video seeking on mobile will be
  broken.
- **Auth/scoping** — artifacts are church content; the serving route must be
  authenticated, project-scoped, and refuse traversal outside the registered root.
- **Whether cloud `/agent-designs` becomes the mirror or is retired** (left open
  by the 2026-07-30 decision).

## Related

- #1306 — generated images do not render in the desktop chat either; the tool
  returns a path with no file attachment. That and this issue share a question:
  what is the canonical reference to an artifact that both clients can resolve?
  Worth solving together.
- #1308 — inbound attachments (mobile → session) need a binary upload endpoint;
  it should write into whatever store this issue picks.
- #1094 / #1304 — the image generation that produces these artifacts.

Supersedes the store choice in
`docs/ai/decisions/2026-07-30-gallery-source-of-truth-is-the-local-mac.md`;
that doc should be marked superseded once this is decided.
title: Artifact hosting: make generated media viewable/downloadable on mobile (supersede the local-only gallery decision)

Vertical slice of #1177 (remote-workspace execution). Product trigger: when away from the main desk but at another computer, continue and manage agent sessions that are running elsewhere.

## Workflow
Operator: the same staff user, on a secondary desktop (not the machine hosting the engine). They list their in-flight/owned sessions, attach to one, observe streamed output, and manage it (send input, approve permissions/questions, cancel) — then the primary desk can pick it back up. Recovery: switching machines or a disconnect resumes the same session, never forks it.

## Acceptance (inherits #1177)
- [ ] From a secondary desktop, the user can enumerate only their own sessions (authenticated, tenant/project-scoped inventory; never arbitrary hosts/roots/worker-supplied authority).
- [ ] Attach delivers streamed messages, tool parts, permissions/questions, terminal output, status, and cancellation through the existing Rhythm surfaces.
- [ ] Session/workspace IDs are opaque and tenant-scoped; cross-user, cross-project, revoked-worker, and stale-token operations fail closed.
- [ ] Two clients on one session don't corrupt state: reconcile ownership/handoff so continuation is idempotent (resume or durable actionable failure, never duplicate/silently abandon).
- [ ] Local execution remains the default and unchanged; the remote-attach capability has an explicit kill switch and disables without data loss.
- [ ] Observability records operator/workspace/session/lifecycle + sanitized failure reason; no credentials, host paths, or transcript content.
- [ ] Negative E2E from a second user/project proves every ID-addressed operation is denied.

Refs #1177
title: OCU-35B/use-case-2: secondary-desktop continuation/management of remote agent sessions

## Problem

Approvals/permissions are spread across **five independent mechanisms** with three different transports, three different auth models, and inconsistent bypass-mode coverage. Bypass mode keeps hitting edge cases, and some approvals can **deadlock with no way to grant them**. This is too complex and keeps regressing.

## Evidence (this session)

1. **Desktop permission reply used the wrong body key** — every approve/deny `POST /agent-sessions/:id/permissions/:id/reply` sent `{response:…}` but the handler reads `{reply:…}`, so it 400'd and the engine stayed blocked; the card re-surfaced forever. Fixed in `9030a6da`, but it only shipped because a test had enshrined the bug.
2. **Security-bound taint approval hangs in bypass mode** (screenshot): an agent in **bypassPermissions** read live PCO data → session tainted → a delegated build required a `#1134` security-bound approval that bypass deliberately does **not** auto-accept. The desktop then couldn't fetch it:
   ```
   [ERROR] Handled UNAUTHORIZED GET /agent-approvals?status=pending — Invalid session token { authUserId: null }
   ```
   `/agent-approvals` uses `requireAuth` and **intentionally does not inherit the AGENT_LOCAL bypass** ("human surfaces never inherit AGENT_LOCAL's internal auth bypass"). The desktop sends a **cloud** bearer (`AuthSessionStore.headers()`) to the **local** server, so a **stale cloud login → `authUserId: null` → 401 → the approval is un-fetchable and un-grantable → permanent hang.**

## The five streams (the mess)

| # | Stream | Transport | Auth | Bypass covers it? | Deadlock risk |
|---|--------|-----------|------|-------------------|---------------|
| 1 | Engine `permission.asked/updated` → bridge auto-accept | WS + engine `/permission/:id/reply` | AGENT_LOCAL / loopback headers | **Yes** (shouldAutoAccept) | reply-key mismatch (fixed) |
| 2 | `#878` bash command classification (hardline deny / ask) | same as #1 | same | partial (hardline never bypasses) | — |
| 3 | `#736` tool-allowlist backstop (role-scoped) | same as #1 | same | n/a (deny only) | — |
| 4 | `#1134` **security-bound taint approvals** (external-data → delegation) | separate `/agent-approvals` REST + `HumanApprovalSigner` | **`requireAuth` real cloud token, NO bypass** | **No** (by design) | **Yes** — 401 on stale token → un-grantable hang |
| 5 | `question.asked` (AskUserQuestion) | separate Question API `/question/:id/reply` | AGENT_LOCAL / loopback | n/a | hang if unanswered |

Five surfaces, inconsistent auth (loopback vs cloud vs Device-token on mobile), inconsistent bypass semantics, and stream #4 can hard-deadlock. A user in "bypass" reasonably expects predictable behavior and instead hits a different failure mode per stream.

## Goals

1. **One coherent approval pipeline / taxonomy.** Two explicit classes: *convenience approvals* (bypass eats them) vs *hardline security controls* (never bypass — prompt-injection defense, taint→delegation, hardline commands). Every approval declares its class; the UI shows which and why.
2. **Consistent, non-deadlocking auth.** A local desktop granting a *local* security approval must not be dead-ended by a stale *cloud* token. Either accept the local human-approval capability signature as sufficient, or fail loudly with "re-login to grant" instead of silently hanging.
3. **Bypass mode has documented, predictable coverage** — one place that decides, not five.
4. **No silent hangs.** Every un-grantable/parked approval surfaces a clear, actionable reason (and, for un-attended/headless sessions, a defined auto-resolution).
5. Collapse the transport surfaces where possible; single source of truth for "is there a pending approval for this session."

## Immediate mitigations (pre-consolidation)

- The current hang: **re-login on the desktop** to refresh the cloud token (the `/agent-approvals` 401 is a stale-session symptom); or cancel the parked session.
- Surface the stale-token case as a visible "sign in again to approve" banner instead of a silent poll 401.
- Document which approval classes bypass cannot eat.

## Scope / sequencing

A comprehensive audit of all five streams is underway (parallel code-mapping). The consolidation design will be appended here. This is **net-new architecture work** — a follow-up workstream; it should **not** block the mega PR merge. Part of the ongoing backlog-burndown effort.
title: Consolidate the fragmented permission/approval streams (bypass edge cases + agent-approvals 401 deadlock)

## Product intent

Recipes should be enforced, durable multi-agent workflow definitions—not prompt snippets stored as JSON.

The implementation should reuse or extract the generic orchestration mechanics already present in `research_project_orchestrator.ts`, including ordered profile-specific stages, per-stage provider/model overrides, durable jobs and restart resume, budgets, critic stages, and synthesis. Do not build a second orchestration engine beside it.

## Target workflow

Support this end-to-end recipe:

1. Planning
2. Cross-provider contrarian review
3. Adjust plan
4. Issue writer
5. Acceptance-contract writer for each emitted issue
6. Coder implementing toward the tests/contract
7. Review against the acceptance contract and plan
8. Coder repair loop
9. Smoke test
10. Failure-triage and repair loop
11. Shippable pull request

Issue-emitting stages must be able to fan out downstream work once per emitted issue.

## Required runner capabilities

- **Explicit stage data flow:** declared inputs from prior stage outputs rather than implicit prompt-history coupling.
- **Profile-specific dispatch:** each stage names its agent profile, with optional provider/model override.
- **Cross-provider contrarian review:** review can intentionally run through a different provider/model from the authoring stage.
- **Structured, fail-closed verdicts:** gates consume a versioned verdict contract; malformed, missing, or ambiguous verdicts do not silently pass.
- **Conditional branches:** route from structured outcomes, including explicit on-fail targets.
- **Bounded loops:** repair/review loops require maximum iteration, cost, token, and wall-clock caps.
- **Fan-out:** dispatch a downstream stage per emitted issue or other structured collection item.
- **Sibling/root dispatch:** orchestrate stages as sibling/root jobs rather than nested delegation-depth chains.
- **Durability:** persist run/job state and resume safely after process restart without replaying completed side effects.
- **Cancellation:** cancel pending/running workflow work and propagate a durable terminal state.
- **Audit trail:** record stage inputs, outputs, selected profile/provider/model, verdicts, transitions, retries, budgets, approvals, and cancellation.
- **Human approval gates:** pause before consequential actions where policy requires approval.

## Schema and compatibility

Define a versioned recipe schema and runner contract before building the editor. Include:

- schema versioning and validation
- migration strategy for current prompt-only recipe rows
- typed stage inputs/outputs and references to prior outputs
- structured branch/gate/verdict definitions
- loop and budget limits
- durable execution identity and idempotency rules

Current prompt-only rows must have an explicit migration path (for example, a compatibility single-prompt stage or a clearly surfaced invalid/upgrade-required state); they must not be silently reinterpreted as fully enforced workflows.

## Flutter UI direction

After the schema/runner contract stabilizes, replace the raw JSON authoring requirement with a vertical step-card editor using standard controls:

- agent dropdown
- optional provider/model override
- inputs selected from prior steps
- gate/verdict configuration
- on-fail target
- maximum iterations and relevant caps

Generate a read-only flow visualization from the configured steps. Do not commit initially to a drag-and-drop canvas; standard form controls are sufficient for the first editor.

The current `agent_cookbook_view.dart` create dialog exposes a monospace **Steps (JSON array)** `TextField`. Users should not need to author raw JSON in the intended UI.

A live-artifact prototype may be useful for validating the editor interaction, but is optional and not a delivery requirement.

## Delivery sequence

1. Specify the versioned recipe schema, stage contracts, verdict contract, durability/idempotency rules, and migration behavior.
2. Reuse/extract generic orchestration primitives from `research_project_orchestrator.ts`.
3. Implement the durable runner, branches, bounded loops, fan-out, cancellation, approvals, and audit trail.
4. Prove the target planning-to-shippable-PR workflow end to end.
5. Build the Flutter step-card editor and generated read-only visualization after the schema stabilizes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A versioned recipe schema expresses the required stages, explicit data flow, gates, branches, caps, and fan-out.
- [ ] The runner reuses/extracts existing research orchestrator mechanics rather than introducing a parallel engine.
- [ ] Structured verdict parsing is fail-closed.
- [ ] All loops enforce iteration, cost, token, and wall-clock limits.
- [ ] Stage dispatch does not consume nested delegation depth across the workflow chain.
- [ ] Runs survive restart, resume idempotently, support cancellation, and expose a complete audit trail.
- [ ] Consequential stages can require durable human approval gates.
- [ ] The target workflow can reach a shippable PR or a bounded, explicit failed/cancelled state.
- [ ] Existing prompt-only recipe rows have tested versioning/migration behavior.
- [ ] Flutter provides a standard-control step-card editor without requiring raw JSON.
- [ ] Flutter generates a read-only flow visualization; drag-and-drop is not required initially.
title: Epic: Recipes as durable, enforced multi-agent workflows

## Observed behavior

An inbound agent webhook can be created and successfully accepts an HMAC-signed payload. The receive endpoint responds with `status: queued`, but the resulting desktop trigger does not provide a usable handoff to an agent:

- The trigger banner has no meaningful task title for a webhook-originated trigger.
- The only available action is **Start Secretary**, regardless of the webhook's configured target scheduled task.
- Starting the agent does not prefill or send the webhook payload, event type, target prompt, or note path.
- The configured target scheduled task/profile is not reflected in the desktop action.

This prevents webhook events from being used for a manual, context-preserving agent handoff.

## Expected behavior

A queued webhook trigger should preserve its configured target and event context through the desktop handoff. When the user starts the trigger, Rhythm should select the configured agent/profile and make the webhook prompt or payload available to that session.

## Reproduction steps

1. Create an agent webhook endpoint with an event allowlist and either a target scheduled task or target prompt.
2. Send a correctly HMAC-SHA256-signed JSON payload to `POST /agent-webhooks/:id/receive`.
3. Confirm the endpoint returns `status: queued`.
4. Leave the authenticated Rhythm desktop app running until its trigger poll completes.
5. Observe the pending-trigger banner.
6. Click **Start Secretary**.
7. Observe that the created session has no webhook payload/prompt context and does not use the configured target profile.

## Impact

Webhook receipt succeeds, but the user cannot act on the event through the desktop trigger without manually reconstructing its missing context.

## Environment notes

- Provider/model/fallback behavior is not involved; the context is lost before an agent turn is sent.
- No usage-limit condition is required to reproduce.
title: Webhook triggers lose payload and only offer Start Secretary

## Request
Unify every Agent Tools page around the layout AJ prefers in Agents → Tasks.

## Reference and shared design contract
AJ explicitly selected **Agents → Tasks** as the visual and interaction reference (not the main Tasks tab). The shared pattern is:
- A compact item list on the left: a simple title and one short subtitle/metadata line.
- Selecting a row opens that item's full details and functions in the main inspector to its right (the center workspace when the app navigation is visible).
- Keep the list for selection; put detailed content, editing, and item-specific actions in the inspector.
- Use the same typography, spacing, row selection, inspector structure, and action placement across these pages. Preserve each domain's actual functions.

## Scope and current evidence
`SessionRail.tsx` lists Brain, Deep Research, Tasks, Webhooks, Profiles, Skills, Playbooks, Cookbook, Review Queue, Report Card, Email, and Gallery. `ToolWorkspace.tsx` contains mixed list, split, report, and gallery presentations; Profiles has its own component. `LiveSchedulesTool` is the reference with `.tool-split`, `.tool-rail`, and `.tool-detail`.

Apply the shared pattern to every tool, including specialized report/artifact views by keeping their detailed content in the inspector. Agent Settings configuration coverage is tracked separately, but must use this same pattern.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Inventory every exposed Tools entry and include an explicit before/after checklist so no tool is missed.
- [ ] Every tool presents selectable compact title/subtitle rows and a main inspector containing the selected item's details and existing functions.
- [ ] Reuse a common layout/row/inspector contract rather than creating page-specific variants of the same pattern.
- [ ] Keep Agents → Tasks as the baseline and preserve its scheduling, history, and action behavior. Do not copy an existing defect merely to achieve visual parity.
- [ ] Preserve specialized editors, artifact previews, review actions, and profile controls within the consistent structure.
- [ ] Mouse and keyboard selection update the correct inspector, with visible focus and selected state.
- [ ] Long titles/metadata, empty results, loading, errors, and read-only access remain usable; resizing does not clip essential controls.
- [ ] Refresh and existing deep links preserve or restore the correct selection; missing/deleted items produce a clear state rather than stale details.

## Likely files
- `apps/web/src/components/ToolWorkspace.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/components/Profiles.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/components/SessionRail.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/components/AgentsWorkspace.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/styles.css`
- `apps/web/src/components/ToolWorkspace.contract.test.mjs` and affected browser tests under `apps/web/tests/`

## Required evaluation
Rendered coverage for selecting two different items on each tool page and reaching existing item actions; representative long-content, empty/error, keyboard, and narrow-window cases. Compare screenshots with Agents → Tasks at identical zoom. Verify affected live-backed actions in an isolated environment; distinguish fixture rendering evidence from live functionality.

## Dependencies / related work
This issue defines the shared UI contract used by the separate Facilities, Messages, Projects, Automations, Integrations, and Agent Settings issues. Coordinate component/style changes. Related reading-comfort issue: #1509; its main Tasks example is not the reference selected here.

## Safety / out of scope
This issue requests Electron/React UI work. Preserve current permissions, confirmations, persisted data, and API contracts. No production data repair, migration, deployment, or automatic execution of user actions is authorized by this design request. Live UI must not silently fall back to fixture-only behavior. Validate any mutations with isolated test data. The mobile bell issue (#1510) and separate Agents sidebar issues (#1511, #1512) remain separate.

## Scope clarification — per-profile editor
AJ clarified that the existing Agents profile page structure is good. Preserve its profile list and selected-profile inspector arrangement; do not restructure it merely for uniformity. The settings/functions UI inside each profile needs a focused redesign, tracked in #1523. Shared typography and component consistency may still apply.

## The user-visible gap

Electron → Agent Settings → **Runtime / OpenCode server** shows two read-only check buttons and a gap notice:

> "Changing or restarting the runtime requires GET and PATCH `/opencode/runtime` plus POST `/opencode/runtime/restart`; those endpoints do not exist."
> — `apps/web/src/components/tools/AgentSettingsTool.tsx:437` (fixture copy at `:118`)

It sends the user to "Flutter Agent settings → OpenCode server".

**That redirect is false and should be fixed regardless of what else is built here.** Flutter has no restart control anywhere. Its "Opencode server" section (`apps/desktop_flutter/lib/features/agents/views/_agent_settings_sheet.dart:394-514`) is a single text field that writes an optional remote URL to `shared_preferences` (`apps/desktop_flutter/lib/features/settings/services/opencode_server_service.dart:10`, key `opencode_server_url`), with "Reset to embedded" clearing it. Flutter's only restart-shaped code is `ApiServerController.retry()` → `initialize()` (`apps/desktop_flutter/lib/app/core/server/api_server_controller.dart:33`), which is the app-launch failure retry, not a settings action.

## Two different runtimes — do not conflate them

The notice's single `/opencode/runtime` hides two processes with different owners:

**1. Local API server, :4001.** Owned by the **Electron main process**, not by itself:
- spawned at `apps/electron/src/agent-server.mjs:337`
- stopped with SIGTERM then SIGKILL at `agent-server.mjs:426-449`
- `agent-server.mjs:388` — *"No automatic restart."*
- `agent-server.mjs:7` — *"Reuse a healthy Rhythm runtime without taking ownership. Only stop children we spawned."*
- renderer bridge already exists: `agentServer.status()` / `onStatusChange` at `apps/electron/src/preload.cjs:32-40`
- an IPC restart precedent already exists in the same file: `hermes.restart()` → `hermes:restart`, `preload.cjs:46`

**2. OpenCode engine, :4096.** Owned by the **api_server**, via `OpencodeClientService`:
- port resolution `apps/api_server/src/services/opencode_client_service.ts:76-99` (default 4096)
- `initialize()` at `:678`, `ensureReady()` at `:648`
- `dispose()` at `:3885` — `server.close()` is documented at `:3866-3876` as the only way to stop the spawned child

## What already exists (the read half is mostly built)

- `GET /opencode/health` — `apps/api_server/src/app.ts:313-315`, payload from `apps/api_server/src/services/opencode_health.ts:11` → `{ status, message, bridgeLive, websearchConfigured }`
- `opencodeClient.getEngineIdentity()` → `{ bootId, pid, version }` (see `apps/api_server/src/contract/issue_1325_engine_respawn.test.ts:17,44`)
- `POST /system/refresh` — `apps/api_server/src/routes/system_routes.ts`, already reloads engine skills and agent-profile config without a restart. **This is the rung below restart and covers most real "the engine is stale" cases.**
- Electron already renders both ports from `gateway.environment` (`apps/web/src/gateway/index.ts:47,147`) and has working liveness check buttons (`AgentSettingsTool.tsx:437`)

So `GET /opencode/runtime` is largely a matter of surfacing `getEngineIdentity()` next to the existing health payload, not new machinery.

## Lifecycle hazard — read before speccing a restart

A naive `POST /opencode/runtime/restart` on :4001 that restarts **:4001** means the api_server tearing down the process tree it is currently serving the request from. The response never lands; the Electron readiness poller sees the socket drop; and the supervisor's failure path escalates to SIGKILL. That is exactly the failure shape behind PR #1508 (idle work blocking the loop → health-poll flap → Retry SIGKILL) and the incident on 2026-09-21. **Do not put an api_server-restart endpoint on the api_server.**

Second hazard: `agent-server.mjs:7` deliberately reuses a healthy runtime it did not spawn. If a Flutter-launched (or `tools/dev/sandbox.sh`-launched) api_server is running, Electron restarting it kills another app's runtime out from under it.

Third: restarting the engine drops in-flight agent turns, the global event stream, and any open permission prompts.

## Proposed split

### A. `GET /opencode/runtime` — read-only, safe, do this first
- **Method/path:** `GET /opencode/runtime`
- **Router:** mount alongside the existing `GET /opencode/health` in `apps/api_server/src/app.ts`, inside the `agentExecutionEnabled` gate, next to the other `/opencode/*` routers. A new router file is not warranted for one read.
- **Response 200:** `{ "engine": { "port": 4096, "pid": 1234, "bootId": "...", "version": "1.14.49", "status": "ready" | "unavailable", "bridgeLive": true }, "api": { "port": 4001 }, "remoteOverride": null }`
- **Auth:** `requireAuth` with the `AGENT_LOCAL=true` bypass, matching `system_routes.ts:32` and `agent_configs_routes.ts:11`. On :4001 the loopback is the trust boundary; on hosted prod a real Bearer token is required.

### B. `PATCH /opencode/runtime` — probably should not exist
The only thing Flutter lets you "change" is the remote OpenCode URL, and that is a **client-side routing preference** stored per device (`opencode_server_service.dart`). Which engine *this client* talks to is not server state; a PATCH to the server asking it to change which server the client uses is incoherent. Port this as an Electron local preference in `apps/web/src/gateway/user-preferences.ts` (see #1550, #1551 for the same store), not as an endpoint. Delete the `PATCH /opencode/runtime` claim from the notice.

### C. Engine restart — scoped to :4096 only
Feasible in-process because the api_server owns the engine child, not itself.
- **Method/path:** `POST /system/restart-engine` — `system_routes.ts` is a better home than a new `/opencode/runtime/*` file: it already owns "make the running engine pick up new state" (`POST /system/refresh`), with the right auth posture and the same `agentExecutionEnabled` mount.
- **Behaviour:** `dispose()` then `initialize()` on `OpencodeClientService`; respond only after `ensureReady()` resolves or a bounded deadline expires.
- **Responses:** `200 { "status": "ready", "bootId": "<new>", "previousBootId": "<old>" }`; `409` when a session has a turn in flight or a permission prompt open, listing what is blocking; `503` with `statusMessage` when the engine does not come back within the deadline.
- **Auth:** same `requireAuth` + `AGENT_LOCAL` bypass as `system_routes.ts:32`.
- **Precondition:** the UI must offer `POST /system/refresh` first and say so — restart is the escalation, not the default button.

### D. Local API-server restart — Electron IPC, never HTTP
- Add `agentServer.restart()` to `apps/electron/src/preload.cjs` beside the existing `status` / `onStatusChange` (`preload.cjs:32-40`), following the `hermes:restart` precedent at `preload.cjs:46`.
- Implement in `apps/electron/src/agent-server.mjs` as stop-then-start of **only** the child it spawned. If the current runtime was adopted rather than spawned (`agent-server.mjs:7`), the call must refuse with a clear reason and the UI must say "this runtime is owned by another app".
- The renderer must expect the gateway to go unreachable and come back, and must not let the readiness poller escalate to a SIGKILL retry during the intended window.

## Electron UI change

In the Runtime inspector, replace the gap notice with, in order: the `GET /opencode/runtime` facts (engine pid / bootId / version / port, API port, remote-override state); the existing liveness check buttons; a **Reload engine config & skills** button on `POST /system/refresh`; then, behind a confirmation naming what will be lost, **Restart engine**; and lastly **Restart local runtime** via IPC, disabled with an explanation when the runtime is not Electron-owned. Remove the "Configure in Flutter Agent settings → OpenCode server" redirect — Flutter cannot do any of this.

## Divergence risk

- **Remote OpenCode URL.** If Electron gets an account-scoped or server-side override while Flutter keeps `shared_preferences['opencode_server_url']`, the two clients silently talk to different engines on the same machine, and the Agent Settings screen will report whichever one it happens to query. Keep it a per-device preference in both clients, as Flutter already does.
- **Restart ownership.** If both Flutter and Electron gain a restart while both can adopt an already-running :4001, each can kill the other's runtime. Ownership must be explicit and the control disabled when the runtime is not ours.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The "Configure this in Flutter Agent settings → OpenCode server" redirect is removed for the runtime section; Flutter does not implement restart and the copy no longer claims it does.
- [ ] `GET /opencode/runtime` returns engine pid, bootId, version, port and status plus the API port, under `requireAuth` with the `AGENT_LOCAL` bypass, and the Electron inspector renders those real values instead of a notice.
- [ ] The Electron inspector offers `POST /system/refresh` as the first-line action and presents restart as an escalation.
- [ ] Engine restart lives in `system_routes.ts`, restarts **only** the :4096 child, never the api_server process itself, and returns a new `bootId` proving the engine actually cycled.
- [ ] Engine restart returns `409` (not a partial teardown) when a turn is in flight or a permission prompt is open, and the UI names what is blocking.
- [ ] Engine restart returns `503` with the engine status message if the engine does not reach ready within a bounded deadline, and the app is still usable afterwards.
- [ ] Local API-server restart is exposed only over Electron IPC, restarts only a child `agent-server.mjs` spawned, and refuses with a stated reason when the runtime was adopted.
- [ ] During an intentional local-runtime restart, the readiness poller does not escalate to the SIGKILL retry path (regression guard for PR #1508 / the 2026-09-21 incident).
- [ ] No `PATCH /opencode/runtime` is added. The remote-URL override, if ported, is a per-device Electron preference in `user-preferences.ts`, matching Flutter's scope.
- [ ] Nothing in this issue restarts a runtime the user did not explicitly ask to restart.

Follow-on to #1514. Related: #1550 (Behavior), #1551 (Keybindings) — same gap notices, same shared_preferences root cause.

## Symptom

Reported by AJ: "there is no way to start a session within a project. I chose the detailed session create button and chose the right file root for the project i am working on, and it still didnt put it in the right session [project]."

A session created through the **Advanced session options** dialog with a correct working directory lands under **No project** in the Agents session list instead of under its project heading.

## How session → project association works today

There is **no project picker anywhere in the create flow**. The web/Electron client never sends `projectId`:

- `apps/web/src/store.tsx:26-38` — `LiveSessionInput` has `name, cwd, profileId, taskId, anthropicAccountId, isolateWorktree, worktreeName, branch, createBranch, stash`. No `projectId` field exists.
- `apps/web/src/components/SessionRail.tsx:168-172` — the advanced dialog submits exactly those fields.
- `apps/web/src/components/SessionRail.tsx:347` — "Working directory" is a free-text input (default: the currently selected session's cwd). The Browse button is disabled in live mode (see #1496).
- `apps/web/src/gateway/sessions.ts:476` — `POST /agent-sessions` with that body.

So the server **infers** the project by cwd prefix:

- `apps/api_server/src/controllers/agent_sessions_controller.ts:935-945` — if the body omits `projectId`, `findByCwdPrefix(sessionCwd)`.
- `apps/api_server/src/repositories/projects_repository.ts:148-166` — longest-prefix match over non-archived `projects.cwd` (trailing slashes stripped; no realpath/symlink resolution, no case folding).

The session list groups purely on that stored `projectId` (`SessionRail.tsx:246-251`), so a null means "No project".

## Root cause

`agent_sessions_controller.ts:943` runs the prefix lookup against **`sessionCwd`**, which at that point is the *isolated worktree directory*, not the file root the user chose.

Order of operations in the create handler:

1. `:868` `const expandedCwd = expandHome(cwd.trim());` — the user's chosen file root.
2. `:908-931` when `isolateWorktree` is true, `opencodeClient.createWorktree(expandedCwd, …)` runs and **`sessionCwd = created.directory`**.
3. `:943` `findByCwdPrefix(sessionCwd)` — matches against the worktree dir.

The opencode engine does **not** put worktrees inside the project directory (the doc comment on `opencode_client_service.ts:2442-2446` claiming "create a worktree in the project directory" is wrong). It puts them under `~/.local/share/opencode/worktree/<repo-hash>/<slug>`, which is not a prefix of any project row, so the lookup returns `null` every time.

### Live evidence (his actual session, API on :4001)

```
createdAt         | projectId | worktreePath / cwd
2026-09-21T19:28  | NULL      | /Users/ajhochhalter/.local/share/opencode/worktree/0174f2e01a6eed09d478703739b5a18499151b52/reload-bug-amazon-misleading-name
```

It is the only row in the most recent 60 sessions with a `worktreePath`, and the only recent interactive session with a NULL `projectId` despite a valid chosen root. Sessions created from the same dialog **without** "Isolate worktree" associate correctly:

```
2026-09-13T02:22 | 35369c67 | /Users/ajhochhalter/Documents/Rhythm
2026-09-14T21:37 | 1e9d6422 | /Users/ajhochhalter/Documents/Encompass H20 2.0/encompass-h2o-web-redesign
```

A project row for the intended root exists and would have matched:
`35369c67 /Users/ajhochhalter/Documents/Rhythm` (`GET /projects?includeArchived=true`).

**Expected:** `projectId = <project whose cwd is a prefix of the *requested* cwd>`.
**Actual:** `projectId = NULL`, because the lookup sees `~/.local/share/opencode/worktree/…`.

## Second defect, same root, same fix

`apps/api_server/src/services/agent_runner.ts:591` hard-codes `projectId: null` on every session it records — it never runs the cwd lookup at all, even for a non-worktree cwd sitting inside a known project. Live evidence: every scheduled/skill run with `cwd = /Users/ajhochhalter/Documents/Rhythm/apps/api_server` has `project_id` NULL, although project `35369c67` covers `/Users/ajhochhalter/Documents/Rhythm`. `agent_runner.ts:996` applies the identical worktree overwrite (`effectiveCwd = created.directory`) before recording.

Both sites should resolve the project from the **requested** project cwd, not the post-worktree cwd. One shared helper covers both callers.

## Reproduction

1. Agents tab → the sliders button beside "New session" (`data-testid="new-session-advanced"`).
2. Working directory: a path inside a known project, e.g. `/Users/ajhochhalter/Documents/Rhythm`.
3. Tick **Isolate worktree**. Create.
4. The new session appears under **No project**.
5. `curl -s localhost:4001/agent-sessions?limit=1` → `projectId: null`, `cwd` under `~/.local/share/opencode/worktree/…`.

Untick "Isolate worktree" and repeat → the session lands under the right project. That is the discriminator.

## Ruled out

- Trailing slashes — `findByCwdPrefix` strips them on both sides (`projects_repository.ts:149-158`).
- `~` expansion — `expandHome` is applied on both create paths (`env.ts:69-73`, `projects_controller.ts:8-23`).
- Client dropping the field — `POST /agent-sessions` returns the persisted row (`agent_sessions_controller.ts:1113`) and the view model reads `projectId` (`gateway/sessions.ts:335`); the stored row itself is NULL.
- Symlinks / `/private/tmp` / case — not implicated in this reproduction (all 17 project rows and his chosen root are plain `/Users/ajhochhalter/...` paths), but note `findByCwdPrefix` does no `realpath`, so a symlinked root would still fail. Worth hardening in the same change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Creating a session with **Isolate worktree** ticked and a cwd inside a known project stores that project's `projectId`; the session appears under that project heading in the rail immediately.
- [ ] Project resolution uses the **requested** cwd, not the worktree directory — both in `agent_sessions_controller.ts` and in `agent_runner.ts` (which must stop hard-coding `projectId: null`).
- [ ] A session created with a cwd under no project still stores `projectId: null` (the No project group keeps working).
- [ ] An explicit `projectId` in the request body still wins, and explicit `null` still means "unassigned".
- [ ] Path matching resolves symlinks (`realpath`) on both the project cwd and the session cwd before comparing, so a symlinked project root associates.
- [ ] Regression test: create with `isolateWorktree: true` against a fixture project root and assert the persisted `project_id`.
- [ ] Stale comment on `opencode_client_service.ts:2442-2446` corrected — worktrees are created under the engine's own storage, not the project dir.

Out of scope: adding a project picker to the dialog — that is the "+" per project heading feature.

## Problem

Requested by AJ: "There should be a little plus button by the project heading in the session list."

Today there is no way to start a session *into* a project. Both create buttons are project-blind:

- `apps/web/src/components/SessionRail.tsx:321` — **New session** (`data-testid="new-chat-instant"`) creates with `cwd: selected.cwd`, i.e. whatever session happens to be selected.
- `apps/web/src/components/SessionRail.tsx:321` — the sliders button (`data-testid="new-session-advanced"`) opens the advanced dialog, whose Working directory field defaults to `selected.cwd` and is free text (`:347`).

Neither sends a `projectId` (`apps/web/src/store.tsx:26-38`). The user has to type the right path and hope the server's cwd-prefix inference picks the project up.

## Requested behavior

A "+" button on each project heading row in the session list (`SessionRail.tsx:326-334`, the `.group-toggle` row), beside the session count.

- Clicking it opens the existing advanced create dialog **pre-filled for that project**: Working directory = the project's `cwd`, and the session created carries that project's id explicitly.
- It must not toggle the group's collapse state (the heading row is currently a single button — the "+" needs to be a sibling control, not nested inside it, or it must `stopPropagation`).
- The created session appears under that project heading, expanded, and selected.
- Keyboard reachable, with an accessible name like "New session in <project name>".

### Sending the project explicitly

Pre-filling the directory is necessary but not sufficient — the client currently has no way to *state* the project. This feature should add `projectId` to `LiveSessionInput` (`apps/web/src/store.tsx:26-38`) and pass it through `gateway.domains.sessions.create` (`apps/web/src/gateway/sessions.ts:113, 476`). The server already honors an explicit `projectId` in the body, including explicit `null` (`apps/api_server/src/controllers/agent_sessions_controller.ts:935-942`) — no API change needed.

### Headings are built from loaded sessions, not from the project list

`SessionRail.tsx:246-251` builds `projectGroups` from the currently loaded session page. A project with no loaded sessions has **no heading**, so it would have no "+". ## Problem

In the **live** `LiveSettingsTool` (`apps/web/src/components/tools/AgentSettingsTool.tsx`), a single failed request destroys the entire Agent Settings surface — including the five sections that did load, and the three that need no network at all.

`load()` fans out with `Promise.allSettled` and keeps the accounts and MCP failures *section-local* (`setAccountsError` / `setMcpError`, lines 168–171), which is the right shape. But the **profiles** rejection is routed to `setError` (line 167), and `error` is handed to `ListInspector` as the `error` prop (line 470).

`ListInspector` treats that prop as fatal for the whole component:

- `ListInspector.tsx:77` — `showList` is forced, and `:156` skips rendering every row when `hasError`
- `ListInspector.tsx:117` — `select()` returns early, so no section can be opened
- `ListInspector.tsx:128` — arrow/Enter keyboard navigation is dead
- `ListInspector.tsx:194` — the inspector pane renders nothing at all

## What the user sees

Reproduced live against the running desktop runtime. When `sessions.profiles()` rejects, the whole page collapses to:

```
Refresh
Session service unavailable          |   Agent settings sections unavailable
```

All seven rows are gone. **Runtime / OpenCode server, Behavior, and Keybindings are unreachable even though none of them make the request that failed** — Runtime in particular is the one place you would go to diagnose a local-runtime problem, and it is the first thing taken away when the local runtime misbehaves.

Two aggravating details in the same state:

1. The request trace bar at the bottom of the page simultaneously reports **"54 agent profiles loaded"** (or "0 agent profiles loaded") while the surface says the sections are unavailable. `setTrace` at `AgentSettingsTool.tsx:173` runs unconditionally with a count derived from a rejected promise, so the footer confidently contradicts the page.
2. There is no per-section retry. The only recovery is the global **Refresh** button, which re-runs all four calls.

## Why it matters

This is the failure mode with the worst timing: it fires exactly when the local runtime is unhealthy, and it removes the diagnostic sections. The Accounts section (rebuilt in `05ca632c`, the quality bar for this surface) already demonstrates the right pattern — its own load failure renders an inline `role="alert"` inside its own inspector and leaves every other section reachable.

Note this is a **shared shell** defect: any `ListInspector` caller that passes `error` gets the same all-or-nothing behaviour, so the fix belongs in `ListInspector` (and/or in how callers classify a partial failure), not in a guard added to Agent Settings alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failure of any one of the four `load()` calls leaves the section list fully rendered and every section selectable.
- [ ] A profiles-load failure is reported **inside the Profiles overview inspector**, in the same inline `role="alert"` shape Accounts already uses — not as the `ListInspector` `error` prop.
- [ ] `ListInspector`'s `error` prop is reserved for "the list itself could not be built". When it is set, document/verify that rows, selection and keyboard navigation are intentionally unavailable; audit the other callers that pass it and move partial failures off it.
- [ ] Runtime / OpenCode server, Behavior and Keybindings remain reachable when every network call fails, since they render no live data.
- [ ] Each section that can fail independently offers its own **Retry** that re-runs only that section's call.
- [ ] The trace footer never reports a success count derived from a rejected promise; on failure it states the failure.
- [ ] Regression coverage: a rendered test that rejects only `sessions.profiles()` and asserts all seven rows are present, the MCP section still opens, and the profiles error is visible in the inspector. (Coverage on this surface is thinner than it looks — the "Agent Settings live persistence" specs shipped without any Playwright config targeting them until `05ca632c`.)

## Likely files

- `apps/web/src/components/tools/AgentSettingsTool.tsx` (lines 157–176, 404–411, 469–470)
- `apps/web/src/components/ListInspector.tsx` (lines 75–77, 116–122, 127–145, 156, 194)

## Out of scope

No change to the gateway, the endpoints, or the error strings the gateway produces. Presentation and reachability only. Does not overlap #1550 / #1551 / #1555, which own the missing behavior/keybindings/runtime endpoints.
title: Electron Agent Settings: one failed request hides all seven sections, including the offline-capable ones

## Problem

Runtime / OpenCode server and Auto-promotion are the two sections that present themselves as `<dl class="property-list">`. Both are hard to read, and both assert state they have not actually verified.

### The property list is 9px right-aligned monospace

`styles.css:386–389`:

```css
.property-list dd { margin: 0; color: var(--fg-2); font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 9px; text-align: right; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
```

Every value in both sections renders at **9px**, monospace, flush right, on a row whose label is flush left. On the Runtime section at 1440px that means the label `Local API` sits at the far left of a ~560px row and `127.0.0.1:4001 · Healthy` sits at the far right — the reader has to traverse the whole row, at the smallest type size in the app, to pair them. (`.list-inspector-row small` and `.kind-badge` are 9px and 8px for the same reason; this issue is about the settings inspector, but the same token choice is worth checking.)

### Runtime says "Not checked" about services the app is already polling

`AgentSettingsTool.tsx:142` initialises both services to `'Not checked'`, and they only change when you press `Check local API` or `Check OpenCode engine` (`:437`). Meanwhile the app chrome at the top of the same window already reads:

```
Environment: Live · API :4001 healthy · Engine :4096 healthy
```

So the section that exists to report runtime health reports **less** than the header bar does, and makes you click two buttons to catch up. On failure, `runRuntimeCheck` (`:310–312`) writes the raw exception message into that same 9px right-aligned mono cell, with no error colour, no `role="alert"`, and nothing announcing it — a failed check and a successful one are typographically identical. Verified live: clicking `Check local API` changed `Not checked` to `Healthy` with zero colour change.

### Auto-promotion asserts a state it failed to load

Observed live: the auto-promotion endpoint is unavailable on this workspace. The card renders:

- a confident `Disabled` badge in the top-right (`AgentSettingsTool.tsx:89`) even though `state` is `null` and nothing is known;
- the failure as plain body text — `Auto-promotion service unavailable Retry` — with `Retry` as an inline `.text-button` jammed against the sentence, no error colour, no icon;
- an `Enable` button that is disabled but still painted in full primary green at `opacity: 0.52`, carrying `title="Requires availability, eligibility, and zero regressions."` — a **wrong explanation**: the real reason is that the service could not be reached.

Its row in the section list is also the **only** one still showing static placeholder copy — "Workspace eligibility and confirmation gates" — while every other row carries live status (`54 configured`, `2 connected · 2 available`, `21 connected · 26 configured`, `API :4001 · engine :4096`). `baseItems` is called at `:404` without an `autoPromotion` key, so nothing tells you from the list that the section is broken.

## Why it matters

These are the two status-reporting sections, and both are currently less trustworthy than the one-line chip in the window chrome. Accounts, the agreed quality bar, states status per record in readable type with a colour treatment for the bad case.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Runtime and Auto-promotion values are legible: no 9px monospace for prose values, and label/value paired closely rather than flung to opposite edges of a wide row.
- [ ] Health status uses a status indicator (colour + text), so healthy / not checked / failed are distinguishable without reading.
- [ ] A failed health check renders as an error (error colour, announced via `role="alert"`) and does not dump a raw exception string into a right-aligned monospace cell.
- [ ] Runtime shows the health the app already knows on open, rather than `Not checked`; the two Check buttons re-verify rather than being the only way to see anything.
- [ ] Auto-promotion does not display an `Enabled`/`Disabled` badge when its state failed to load; it shows an unknown/unavailable state instead.
- [ ] The toggle's `title` explains the actual blocking reason, and does not claim an eligibility failure when the cause is an unreachable service.
- [ ] The Auto-promotion row in the section list carries live status like the other six, including an error state.
- [ ] The failure + `Retry` is a proper error block with a real button, matching the other sections' error affordances.

## Likely files

- `apps/web/src/components/tools/AgentSettingsTool.tsx:82–90` (`AutoPromotionSettings`), `:142`, `:304–314` (`runRuntimeCheck`), `:404–411` (`baseItems`), `:437` (`runtimeInspector`)
- `apps/web/src/styles.css:386–389` (`.property-list`), `:728–734` (`.auto-promotion-card`)
- `apps/web/src/components/tools/AgentSettingsTool.css:133–150`

## Out of scope

Does not overlap #1555, which owns the missing runtime **control** endpoints (restart / reconfigure). This issue is only about how the existing read-only status is presented.
title: Electron Agent Settings: Runtime and Auto-promotion report status in 9px right-aligned mono and assert state they never verified

## Problem In the **live** `LiveSettingsTool` (`apps/web/src/components/tools/AgentSettingsTool.tsx`), in-flight state is tracked with one free-form string, `pendingAction` (`:143`), and the sentinel written by each handler does not match the prefix the UI tests for. `mcpInspector` gates its only progress indicator on `pendingAction.startsWith('mcp-')` (`:441`): ```jsx {pendingAction.startsWith('mcp-') &&

Saving MCP configuration…

} ``` But the three most-used MCP handlers write sentinels that do not start with `mcp-`: | handler | line | sentinel written | matches `mcp-`? | |---|---|---|---| | `runMcpAction('connect')` | 322 | `` `connect-${server.name}` `` | **no** | | `runMcpAction('disconnect')` | 322 | `` `disconnect-${server.name}` `` | **no** | | `removeMcp` | 340 | `` `remove-${server.name}` `` | **no** | | `addMcp` | 352 | `mcp-add` | yes | | `saveMcpCredentials` | 365 | `` `mcp-credentials-${name}` `` | yes | | `startMcpOAuth` / `checkMcpOAuth` | 377 / 389 | `mcp-oauth-…` | yes | Meanwhile **every** button in the section is disabled by the truthiness of the same string — `disabled={Boolean(pendingAction)}` appears on every control in the Accounts, provider, MCP and Runtime inspectors. ### What the user sees Clicking `Connect`, `Disconnect` or `Remove` on any MCP server: every button on the page goes flat and unclickable, nothing spins, nothing says anything, and the page sits silent until the request returns. There is no way to tell whether the click registered, and the disabled state is indistinguishable from the disabled state a `needsCredentials` server already has. `Add server` and `Save credentials` do show the status line — so the section is inconsistent with itself. ### Second problem: the notice is shared across sections `actionNotice` (`:144`) is a single string, rendered in **both** `accountsInspector` (`:418`) and `mcpInspector` (`:442`), and it is never cleared on section change. Disconnect an MCP server, switch to Accounts, and Accounts displays "`propresenter` disconnected." as if it were an Accounts result. Nothing clears it but the next action. `accountsInspector` has the mirror of the first bug at `:417` — it tests `startsWith('account-')` / `startsWith('provider-')`, which its handlers do honour, so Accounts works; MCP is where the convention broke. ## Why it matters Disabling every control with no indication of why is the worst of both: the UI looks broken rather than busy. And a success notice appearing under an unrelated section is actively misleading about what just happened. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Connect, Disconnect and Remove on an MCP server show in-flight feedback, at minimum the same `role="status"` line the add/credentials flows already show. - [ ] Replace the string-prefix convention with something that cannot silently drift — e.g. `{ scope: 'mcp' | 'accounts' | 'runtime', key: string }` — so a new handler cannot fail to match a prefix. - [ ] In-flight state disables only the controls it actually affects (ideally the acting row plus destructive actions), not every button in every section. - [ ] The acting control itself shows a busy state rather than merely going flat. - [ ] Action notices are scoped to the section that produced them and are cleared when the selected section changes. - [ ] Rendered regression coverage: assert the status line appears during an MCP disconnect, and that an MCP notice is not visible after switching to Accounts. ## Likely files - `apps/web/src/components/tools/AgentSettingsTool.tsx:143–144, 186–398 (all handlers), 414–453 (both inspectors)` ## Out of scope No change to the MCP or account endpoints or to what the handlers do on success/failure. Feedback and enablement only.

body:
## Question

"Is there a way to make Hermes and Rhythm share the same memory and account credentials (OpenAI, Anthropic etc.) so it is one AI settings screen, and whatever is accessible on one is accessible on the other?"

Three sub-questions with three different answers. Short version:

| | Answer |
|---|---|
| **Credentials** | **Partly — and one provider is already shared without anyone noticing.** Share via `~/.hermes/.env` for API keys. Never write `~/.hermes/auth.json`. Never share an OAuth refresh token. |
| **Memory** | **Neither system adopts the other — they were already designed to converge on the Obsidian vault.** The blocker is a path default (being fixed separately). What is left to design is concurrent-write safety in a directory two processes now share. |
| **One AI settings screen** | **Yes** — Rhythm's Accounts page, as a *view over two stores*, not a merge of them. |

Investigation was read-only. No credential value was read, printed or copied; no `auth.json` or memory file was modified.

---

## Current-state map

### Hermes — `$HERMES_HOME/auth.json` (default `~/.hermes/auth.json`)

Source read at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/` — the install ships its own Python source, so this is all verifiable on disk.

Envelope: `version`, `updated_at`, `active_provider`, `providers{}`, `credential_pool{}`.

- `hermes_cli/auth.py::_save_auth_store` — read-modify-write under `~/.hermes/auth.lock`, atomic `O_EXCL` tmp + rename, `0600`, parent dir tightened to `0700`. It loads the whole dict and mutates one provider subtree, so unknown top-level keys survive a write.
- `hermes_cli/auth.py::_load_auth_store` — **unreadable** (EACCES/EMFILE) raises deliberately, so a later save cannot erase the store. **Unparseable** copies to `auth.json.corrupt` and returns an *empty* store. A malformed or half-written file from an outside writer therefore costs the user every Hermes credential on the next save.
- `HERMES_HOME` (`hermes_constants.py`) selects the store. 16 profiles exist under `~/.hermes/profiles/*`, each with its own `auth.json`; `_global_auth_file_path` gives a profile a **read-only fallback** to the root store, per provider.
- `~/.hermes/shared/` is *not* a sharing surface — it contains one empty lock file.

Providers relevant to the overlap (`PROVIDER_REGISTRY`):

| Hermes id | auth_type | env vars checked |
|---|---|---|
| `anthropic` | api_key | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` |
| `gemini` | api_key | `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` |
| `openai-api` | api_key | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `openai-codex` | oauth_external | — (own grant, own refresh) |
| `openrouter` | api_key | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| `nous` | oauth_device_code | — |

### Rhythm — `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`

Flat map. `anthropic | google | openai → {type, access, expires, refresh}`; `openrouter | ollama-planner | ollama-executor → {type, key}`. Existing machinery: `anthropic_accounts_service.ts` / `anthropic_accounts_store.ts` (multi-account, `ok` / `needs_relogin`), `credentials_bridge_service.ts` (15-min re-bridge + change-gated Keychain poll), `auth_credential_watcher.ts`, `opencode_auth_routes.ts`, and the vendored `rhythm-anthropic-accounts` plugin.

A symlink cannot work — the shapes differ and Hermes' envelope is versioned.

---

## Finding 1 — Anthropic is already shared. There is nothing to build.

`agent/credential_pool.py::_sync_anthropic_entry_from_credentials_file` re-reads the external Claude Code credential on every use of an `anthropic` pool entry whose `source == "claude_code"`, and adopts a changed access **or** refresh token. Its own docstring:

> "OAuth refresh tokens are single-use. When something external (e.g. Claude Code CLI, or another profile's pool) refreshes the token, it writes the new pair to `~/.claude/.credentials.json`. The pool entry's refresh token becomes stale. This method detects that and syncs."

`agent/anthropic_adapter.py::read_claude_code_credentials` reads **both** the macOS Keychain item `Claude Code-credentials` **and** `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, reconciling by preferring the non-expired one, else the later `expiresAt`. Rhythm's `credentials_bridge_service` already runs a change-gated Keychain poll against the same credential.

So for Anthropic both apps are already downstream of one shared upstream. The gap is that no screen says so.

> **Caveat to close first:** a classifier denied the grep that would have re-confirmed the Keychain item name on Rhythm's side (`credentials_bridge_service.ts`, `auth_credential_watcher.ts`). That half is taken from the existing project description, not re-verified in this investigation. Confirm it as step one — if Rhythm polls a *different* Keychain item, this finding weakens from "the same entry" to merely "both read the keychain".

## Finding 2 — env injection does not work today, and fails silently

`apps/electron/src/hermes-server.mjs` spawns Hermes with `childBaseEnv = { ...env }`, so Rhythm can already set any variable. But API-key resolution goes through `hermes_cli/config.py::get_env_value_prefer_dotenv`, which reads `~/.hermes/.env` **before** `os.environ`, by design:

> "a deliberate edit to `.env` must take precedence over a stale value inherited from the parent shell (Codex CLI, test scripts, login profile exports)."

`~/.hermes/.env` exists on this machine (24 KB) and already defines `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `GOOGLE_API_KEY` — the two providers that overlap most. Anything Rhythm injects for those is silently ignored. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is *not* in the file, so injection would appear to work there today and would break the day the user adds it.

**`.env` is the layer to write, not the environment.**

## Finding 3 — the dual-refresher hazard, and why it is narrower than it looks

Hermes has already shipped this bug internally and documents it at `agent/credential_pool.py::_write_through_provider_state_to_global_root`: `nous`, `openai-codex` and `xai-oauth` rotate the refresh token on refresh, so a profile that refreshes a grant read from the root store must write the rotated chain back —

> "Otherwise root keeps a now-revoked refresh token and every other profile reading the stale root grant dies with `refresh_token_reused` / `invalid_grant` once its access token expires."

That is exactly what a naively shared `auth.json` would produce between Rhythm and Hermes: random logouts — strictly worse than the status quo.

It is survivable only because the providers Rhythm holds as OAuth have no independently-refreshing Hermes counterpart:

- **anthropic** — api_key-typed in Hermes; `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is consumed as a static bearer. The only refresh path is the `source="claude_code"` sync above, which *adopts* from the shared file rather than racing it.
- **google** — Hermes' `gemini` is api_key only. Rhythm's Google OAuth refresh token has no Hermes counterpart at all.
- **openrouter** — static key, no refresh.
- **openai** — Hermes' `openai-codex` is a *different grant* from Rhythm's `openai`. Do not cross them.

**Rule that follows: share access tokens and API keys. Never write a refresh token into Hermes.**

---

## Recommended design

Smallest thing that works, in order. Nothing here needs an upstream Hermes change.

1. **Anthropic: surface, don't sync.** A read-only "also used by Hermes (shared Claude Code credential)" line on the Accounts page. Zero moving parts.
2. **API-key providers: Rhythm writes `~/.hermes/.env`.** One flat `KEY=value` file, no schema to version, and it is the layer Hermes consults first. Map Rhythm's provider → Hermes' documented env var name (table above). Atomic tmp+rename at `0600`, preserving every line, comment and ordering Rhythm did not write.
3. **Never open `~/.hermes/auth.json` for writing.** Read it only to *display* what Hermes has. Justification: an unparseable store silently becomes empty, and its provider subtrees hold rotating grants Rhythm does not own.
4. **If a provider is only reachable via `auth.json`,** shell out to `hermes auth` rather than writing the file — the CLI takes the lock and writes the current schema.

### Conflict resolution — stated, not implied

Rhythm owns only the keys it wrote, tracked in a Rhythm-side manifest. On write it may replace a `.env` key that is absent or that Rhythm previously wrote. A key present in `.env` that Rhythm did not write is **user-established in Hermes**: leave it, show it on the Accounts page as "set in Hermes — not managed here", and offer an explicit "take over" action. No silent overwrite, ever.

### Failure modes

- **Sync fails** → Hermes keeps its previous `.env` value. Stale credentials in one app; fails closed.
- **Token refreshes** → only API keys are synced, and API keys do not refresh. The Anthropic path self-heals from the shared Keychain credential.
- **User logs out in Rhythm** → Rhythm removes only the keys it owns. Hermes falls back to whatever else it has.
- **User logs out in Hermes** → Rhythm's store is untouched. Asymmetric on purpose: Rhythm is the source of truth for what it wrote, and for nothing else.
- **Hermes changes its schema** → see the update-interaction section. `.env` has no schema, which is most of why it is the recommended surface.

---

## Memory — the question mostly dissolves; what is left is concurrent writes

The follow-up question was: *"seems like it would be easier to adopt the Hermes memory system with Rhythm than the Rhythm system with Hermes?"*

**Neither, and the premise doesn't hold.** Both tools were already designed to converge on one place, and they already name it:

- Hermes' own `~/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md` opens with: *"Obsidian is AJ's core long-term memory. Vault: `~/Documents/Obsidian Vault`. Keep Hermes MEMORY/USER lean; substantive outputs go to vault."* Hermes explicitly disclaims owning long-term memory.
- Rhythm's `apps/api_server/src/config/env.ts:98` documents the intended production setting in its own comment: `MEMORY_VAULT_PATH="~/Documents/Obsidian Vault/AGENT-MEMORY"` with `MEMORY_VAULT_SUBDIR=""`.

So there was never a "which system wins" question. The defect is that Rhythm isn't reaching the agreed location: `env.ts:83` and `env.ts:613` hard-code the fallback `'~/Documents/Memory-Vault'`, the packaged app sets neither env var, and the running app logged `vault=/Users/ajhochhalter/Documents/Memory-Vault` (89 notes) while the real vault at `Obsidian Vault/AGENT-MEMORY` holds 376. **A separate agent is fixing the path default and merging the stale notes right now — that work is in flight and is not part of this issue.** Referenced here only because it is the precondition for everything below.

Worth recording for whoever adjudicates: neither system is a candidate to absorb the other anyway.

| | Hermes (`tools/memory_tool.py`, `MemoryStore`) | Rhythm (`apps/api_server/src/services/memory_*`) |
|---|---|---|
| Shape | 2 files, `§`-delimited entries, no frontmatter, no ids | Typed notes, YAML frontmatter (`kind`, `source`, `source_id`, `created`, `updated`), kind-folders |
| Size | Hard caps: `memory_char_limit=2200`, `user_char_limit=1375` — **3,575 chars total** | 376 notes and growing |
| Retrieval | **None.** `add`/`replace`/`remove`/`apply_batch`; substring matching. Whole store injected verbatim into the system prompt as a frozen snapshot at session start | Lexical + semantic rank fusion (`fuseMemoryRanks`), relevance floor `0.60`, link expansion, budgeted preface (2 items / 1200 chars / ~300 tokens) |
| Scope | Per-profile — each of 16 profiles has its own 3.5 KB store | One vault |

Hermes' side is small **on purpose** — the frozen snapshot exists to preserve the prefix cache for the whole session, and the char caps are what bound that prompt cost. It is a working set, not a store. Rhythm's is the store. They are complementary, which is what the MEMORY.md preamble already says.

### Does Hermes actually write to the vault today?

**Not programmatically — and this is the finding that sizes the risk.** `~/.hermes/config.yaml` contains no vault path, no Obsidian reference and no Obsidian MCP server; there is no Obsidian skill or plugin under `~/.hermes/skills` or `~/.hermes/plugins`. The MEMORY.md line is a *prompt instruction to the model*, not a configured integration. So Hermes reaches the vault only when an agent decides to, using generic file tools, with no format discipline and no locking.

That makes the collision risk **real but bursty and unstructured**, which is worse to design for than a steady programmatic writer: the writes are unpredictable in timing, in path, and in shape.

### Concurrent writes — now the headline risk

Rhythm's protection is **in-process only**. `memoryVaultWriteService.ts:1047` keeps `lifecycleMutationTails`, a JS `Map<string, Promise<void>>` that serialises read-modify-write per note path inside one Node process. Individual note writes are atomic on disk (`.{name}.rhythm-{hex}.tmp` → `fs.rename`, lines 477–499). But there is **no advisory lock, no lockfile, nothing another process can observe**. Two Rhythm processes, or Rhythm plus a Hermes agent, have zero coordination.

Hermes does have a locking convention — `~/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md.lock`, `USER.md.lock`, plus `_detect_external_drift`, which quarantines a foreign edit to a `.bak` rather than merging it — but that convention lives in `MemoryStore` and applies to its own two files. Nothing carries it into the vault.

**Recommendation: sidecar lockfiles, and only where a read-modify-write happens.**

- Per-note writes are already atomic via tmp+rename. A clobber is possible (last writer wins) but a torn file is not. Leave them.
- Read-modify-write paths (`mutateMemoryLifecycle`, merge-on-capture, and the aggregate regeneration below) take a `<path>.lock` — same convention Hermes already uses — held for the read *and* the write, with a short timeout and a fail-closed abort. Match Hermes' naming so any future Hermes-side integration interoperates for free.
- Add drift detection on the Rhythm side mirroring Hermes': if a note's mtime/digest changed between read and write, abort and re-read rather than overwrite. This is the cheap, correct guard against an agent having hand-edited the note in the meantime.

### Format compatibility — let them coexist, don't unify

**Do not force a common note format.** They are different shapes serving different jobs, and a shared tree tolerates that fine:

- Rhythm owns `AGENT-MEMORY/<kind>/<slug>.md` — typed, frontmattered, generated.
- Hermes' `MEMORY.md` / `USER.md` stay under `~/.hermes/memories/`. They are per-profile and capped; they do not belong in the vault.
- Agent-authored vault notes (the "substantive outputs go to vault" path) are ordinary Obsidian markdown. Rhythm's indexer should treat a note **without** recognised frontmatter as an untyped vault note — index it for retrieval, never rewrite it, never enrol it in the lifecycle. Frontmatter presence is the ownership marker.

Inventing a third schema both must serve is the expensive answer to a problem neither tool has.

### Whose index wins

`AGENT-MEMORY/index.md` and `log.md` are generated aggregates and will fight if two writers regenerate them. **Rhythm owns both, exclusively.** Nothing in Hermes generates either today, so this costs nothing to declare now and is much harder to retrofit later. Write it down in the vault itself — a short `AGENT-MEMORY/README.md` stating that `index.md` and `log.md` are machine-generated by Rhythm and must not be hand-edited — because the other writer here is a language model reading the directory.

### Is the provenance/audit trail load-bearing, or write-only bookkeeping?

**Load-bearing.** `log.md` has two non-test consumers — `memoryVaultWriteService.ts` and `memory_consolidation_drafter.ts`. The drafter *reads* it, so consolidation quality depends on it. `source` / `source_id` frontmatter is likewise consumed by the lifecycle and merge-on-capture paths (`memory_lifecycle_index`, `memory_update_by_db_id`, `memory_merge_on_capture`). This is not decoration, and it is the concrete thing that would have been destroyed had Rhythm adopted Hermes' flat format.

## One AI settings screen

Yes. Rhythm's Accounts page (rebuilt in `05ca632c`) is the right home. It becomes a **view over two stores**, not a merge:

- **Reads** Rhythm's own store; `~/.hermes/.env` key *names*; and `~/.hermes/auth.json`'s `version`, `providers` keys and `credential_pool` keys — to show what Hermes has that Rhythm does not.
- **Writes** only `~/.hermes/.env`, and only keys it owns.
- **Shows, per provider**: which side holds a credential, and the source — Rhythm store / Hermes `.env` / Hermes `auth.json` / shared Claude Code Keychain.

---

## Interaction with in-place Hermes updates — read before implementing either issue

If Hermes becomes independently updatable, it can change `auth.json`'s envelope (`version`, `providers`, `credential_pool`, `active_provider`) underneath Rhythm without a Rhythm release.

Any read of `auth.json` **must branch on `version` and fail closed** — render "Hermes credential store version N is newer than this build understands" and show nothing, rather than guess at a layout. This is the strongest single argument for the `.env` recommendation above: `.env` is a flat key/value file with no schema to version, so it cannot drift.

---

## Upstream Hermes changes — not required, but worth filing upstream

Neither is a blocker; both would make this first-class instead of inferred:

1. A `source="rhythm"` external-file sync for `anthropic` pool entries, mirroring the existing `source="claude_code"` one.
2. A `HERMES_ENV_FILE` override, or a designated set where `os.environ` wins over `.env`, so a host app can inject credentials without editing the user's `.env`.

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Keychain-item link in Finding 1 is confirmed (or refuted) against Rhythm's `credentials_bridge_service.ts` before anything is built on it.
- [ ] Rhythm never opens `~/.hermes/auth.json` for writing. A test asserts this.
- [ ] The Accounts page lists, per provider, which of Rhythm / Hermes holds a credential and names the source.
- [ ] Setting an API key in Accounts writes it to `~/.hermes/.env` under Hermes' documented env var name, and it takes effect in Hermes on next start.
- [ ] A `.env` key Rhythm did not write is shown as Hermes-owned and is never replaced without explicit confirmation.
- [ ] Removing a credential in Rhythm removes only Rhythm-written `.env` keys.
- [ ] `.env` writes are atomic (tmp + rename), `0600`, and preserve every unrelated line, comment and ordering.
- [ ] Reading `~/.hermes/auth.json` with an unrecognised `version` degrades to "unknown" per provider; it never throws and never writes.
- [ ] No refresh token is ever written into any Hermes store.
- [ ] No credential value is logged, sent to production, or included in diagnostics.
Memory (all of these assume the in-flight vault-path fix has landed; none of them duplicate it):

- [ ] Rhythm's read-modify-write vault paths take a `<path>.lock` sidecar, matching Hermes' existing `MEMORY.md.lock` naming, held across read and write, with a timeout and a fail-closed abort.
- [ ] A note whose digest changed between read and write aborts and re-reads rather than overwriting. A test simulates an external edit mid-mutation.
- [ ] A vault note without recognised frontmatter is indexed for retrieval and never rewritten or enrolled in the lifecycle.
- [ ] `AGENT-MEMORY/index.md` and `log.md` are declared Rhythm-owned, and an `AGENT-MEMORY/README.md` says so in the tree itself.
- [ ] Hermes' `MEMORY.md` / `USER.md` stay under `~/.hermes/memories/`; nothing in this work writes into `~/.hermes`.
- [ ] No Hermes SQLite file (`state.db`, `projects.db`, `kanban.db`, `verification_evidence.db`, `cron/*.db`) is read or written. Those are operational state, not memory, and carry live WAL files.
